decisions.label: Overlap I/O
decisions.brief: Off: the experts are computed on the device, beside its cache.
decisions.reason: overlap hides the CPU's expert compute behind the streamer's reads, and with the device expert cache armed the experts are computed on CUDA0, so there is nothing on the CPU for it to hide

decisions.label: Device expert cache
decisions.brief: A 6.0 GiB cache of the most used experts on CUDA0, in place of whole layers' experts.
decisions.reason: the experts used most live on the processor that computes them fastest, as the RAM cache holds what flash would read: CUDA0 computes this model's experts at 180 GiB/s against the host's 21, both measured on this model's own expert block; a cache of 6114 MiB (6075 the capacity fitter gave 9 of 48 layers' experts, 39 it left free under one more whole layer) serves 19% of a token's routed bytes (the fraction of the expert set it holds); a miss is uploaded from the host

decisions.label: Batch width
decisions.brief: 2048 tokens per pass; wider would take 6.5 GiB of the device's memory.
decisions.reason: a graph as wide as the context would reserve 6644 MiB of compute buffers on the devices, more than 10% of the 11904 MiB of device memory, where the model does not fit whole; at 2048 tokens it is 634 MiB. A prompt takes more passes and the expert cache keeps the rest: a prompt is paid once and a token every time. --ubatch sets it by hand

decisions.label: Layer placement
decisions.brief: 49 layers on a device; 48 of 48 layers keep their experts on the CPU.
decisions.reason: the capacity fitter found a placement that is projected to fit; 48 of 48 MoE layers keep their experts on the host, host-resident 116 MiB, on devices 4644 MiB, context 16384 (fitter's host breakdown: model 53830, context 0, compute 116 MiB; file 63336, experts 32400)

decisions.label: Context
decisions.brief: 16384 tokens of context, as given: not weighed against the cache.
decisions.reason: the value this run was given, not a choice: the capacity fitter only picks a context when it is handed a zero and this planner always pins it, so nothing has weighed this number against what the memory it reserves would buy as expert cache

decisions.label: Streaming mode
decisions.brief: The whole model (32.7 GiB) fits in the 74.4 GiB usable.
decisions.reason: on the host 33466 MiB (dense 1066) against 76215 MiB usable, which is the 95269 MiB this process may hold (as reported available, unmeasured) less a 19053 MiB margin (the process is killed)

decisions.label: Experts in a device's host memory
decisions.brief: The experts copied into CUDA0's own host memory, for the cache's misses.
decisions.reason: a miss reaches CUDA0 at 9.9 GiB/s from the file's mapping and at 21.4 from the backend's own host memory; the copy takes 32400 MiB, inside the 76215 MiB the host may hold with the 33466 MiB it already does

decisions.label: Expert streaming
decisions.brief: Not streamed: the whole model fits in memory.
decisions.reason: the host residual fits: llama.cpp's placement is the whole plan

decisions.label: Compute threads
decisions.brief: 8 threads: the fastest count measured on this model's format.
decisions.reason: swept over the thread counts this machine has, on a matmul in this model's own quantized format, which is the material that matters: a sweep in F32 can pick a count the quantized kernels are much slower at

decisions.label: Thread counts to measure
decisions.brief: The first answer measures 6 and 12 threads against 8.
decisions.reason: the thread count changes no output and which one decodes fastest is this machine's answer, not a rule's: once the cache has settled the first real request alternates decode windows between 8 and 6 and 12 (where a slower class of core starts, every core, or half of them where all are alike), and switches only to a count 10% faster in the median of its rounds; the next load starts from the verdict
